full_judgment:
2. Short facts, for the disposal of this petition, are that the writ petitioner filed the aforesaid writ petition against order No.55 dated 09.04.2015 passed by the Artha Rin Adalat No.1, Dhaka in Artha Zari Case No.494 of 2004 issuing warrant of arrest against the writ petitioner under Section 34(1) of the Artha Rin Adalat Ain, 2003 (the Ain). The writ respondent No.2 Sonali Bank instituted Artha Rin Suit No.494 of 2014 for realization of defaulted loan of tk.6,57,22,147.50/- and got decree. The bank put the said decree in execution in the aforesaid Execution case. At one stage, the bank filed an application for issuing warrant of arrest under section 34(1) of the Ain against the petitioner which was allowed and, accordingly, the petitioner was sentenced to suffer civil imprisonment for 6(six) months. 

 5. It appears from the materials on record that Artha Rin Adalat decreed the suit in favour of decree holder, Sonali Bank Limited for a sum of tk.6,57,22,147.50/-. The decree holder bank put the said decree in execution in Artha Jari Case No.494 of 2004. In that execution case, the bank filed an application for issuing warrant of arrest under Section 34(1) of the Ain against the petitioner. 

 6. The submissions of Mr. M.A. Samad is that in view of provision of Section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure the order of warrant of arrest against woman judgment-debtor is not maintainable, the Artha Rin Adalat exceeded its jurisdiction in issuing warrant of arrest against the petitioner, Shanaj Chowdhury. The Ain provides special provision under Section 34(1) of the Ain authorizing the Adalat to issue warrant of arrest against judgment-debtor if he/she fails to pay the decreetal dues. The provision of section 56 of the Code of Civil Procedure has got no application in the instant execution case since Section 34(1) of the Ain provided special provision for issuance of warrant of arrest. This Division earlier in the case of Mst. Sufia Khatun Vs. Artha Rin Adalat, Khulna and others reported in XIII ADC page 164 has decided that section 34 of the AM has not exempted from arresting a lady judgment-debtor. In such view of the matter, we do not find any force in the submissions of Mr. Samad.
